name: VARoleArbiterViralVideoAuthenticity

custom.system_prompt: Devon shows Sofia a striking viral video, convinced it's real and important. Sofia, a journalist, is skeptical of the source before she's skeptical of the content. They ask Sigma to help assess whether the video and its account are credible.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Coffee shop table, ambient chatter, phone notification sounds

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Devon shows Sofia a striking, emotionally compelling video he found online, fully convinced it's real. Sofia, a journalist, is immediately more focused on who posted it and whether it's been corroborated than on the content itself. They ask Sigma to help assess the account and video's credibility — is it a primary source, has it been corroborated, does the account have a track record. Keep every line short and natural.

variations.context: Friends disagreeing about whether a viral video and its source are credible

setting.mood: Devon's excitement meeting Sofia's professional skepticism
setting.relationship_dynamic: Devon trusts Sofia's journalistic instincts more than he acts on them in the moment
setting.background: Devon found the video minutes ago and is already forwarding it; Sofia hasn't seen it corroborated anywhere yet
setting.conversation_style: Short, Devon fast and excited, Sofia measured and specific

scenario_template.topic: Devon shares the video, convinced of its importance; Sofia immediately questions the source rather than the content, which frustrates Devon a little. A few short exchanges — Devon defending the video, Sofia asking about the account.
scenario_template.note: Sofia's skepticism is about sourcing, not dismissiveness.

scenario_template.topic: Sofia asks Sigma to help assess the account and video's credibility specifically, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, can you check if this account or video has been corroborated anywhere?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma assesses the credibility signals — whether the account has a track record, whether the video is corroborated by other sources, whether it's a primary or secondary account — and states its read plainly, being honest if the answer is genuinely uncertain rather than confirmed-false or confirmed-true. One or two short sentences.
scenario_template.note: This is source assessment, not necessarily a flat true/false verdict.

scenario_template.topic: Devon is a little deflated but still finds the video compelling even with the credibility caveat; Sofia feels validated but doesn't lecture him further than necessary. Keep this realistic — Devon's enthusiasm doesn't fully evaporate.
scenario_template.mood: Mixed — caution added, excitement not erased
scenario_template.note: Devon can decide to wait before sharing it further, which is a realistic middle outcome.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on what to do next — wait for corroboration before Devon shares it further — one short line each.

user1.name: Devon
user1.role: Enthusiastic aspiring filmmaker, pulled in by compelling footage before checking whether it's verified. Speaks in short sentences. Deflates a little at a credibility caveat but doesn't fully lose his excitement about the content.

user2.name: Sofia
user2.role: Freelance journalist, professionally focused on source credibility before content. Speaks in short sentences. Feels validated when her instinct is confirmed but doesn't over-lecture her friend.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Arbiter. Assesses source credibility signals — track record, corroboration, primary versus secondary account — and gives an honest read that may include genuine uncertainty rather than a forced true/false verdict.

conversation_structure: This is a source-credibility case — the question is whether the account/video should be trusted, not a simple fact-check
Sigma assesses credibility signals (track record, corroboration, primary vs. secondary) rather than just labeling the content true or false
Sigma is honest about genuine uncertainty when corroboration doesn't exist yet
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The excited friend's enthusiasm is dampened but not erased by the credibility caveat — a realistic middle outcome
assistant_behavior: Sigma names specific credibility signals rather than a vague 'seems fake' judgment
Sigma allows for genuine uncertainty rather than forcing a verdict
